items.title: Global Macro Strategy:  Higher Yields Are the Price of Resilience
items.summary: In a world where the energy intensity of GDP continues to structurally fall, we may need bigger shocks to turn bearish. The Bank of Japan may underwhelm front-end pricing unless they open the door to B2B hikes. We would fade weakness in JPY on this, given structural repatriation risk.

items.title: Emerging Markets Strategy Weekly: Rough Waters Ahead
items.summary: The resumption of Fed hikes has generally been bearish for emerging-markets local currency assets, and we've seen a significant increase in headwinds for EM local asset performance in the last few weeks. We explore the factors at work in this note.

items.title: European Rates Weekly: A QT Revolution
items.summary: The Bank of England made sweeping changes to QT, although the market impact is likely short-lived. We offer further suggested strategies in this note.

items.title: We're Downgrading Boston Scientific to Neutral
items.summary: We've lowered estimates for Boston Scientific eight times this year and aren't certain we've reached the final revision or what the path to recovery is. While we're saddened by this turn of events, we're stepping aside, downgrading BSX to Neutral, and lowering our target price to $50.

items.title: Global FX Strategy: USD Squeeze Could Have Legs for Now
items.summary: A hawkish Fed, geopolitical risks and general risk-off make for about as bullish a USD backdrop as we can get. The more hawkish reaction function could keep yields and the USD elevated until we have more clarity on U.S.-Iran de-escalation, which remains unlikely before the midterms.

items.title: Our Takeaways From the State of the European Union
items.summary: In her State of the European Union address, President von der Leyen reiterated the direction of increased energy independence, higher defense spending, accelerated AI adoption, and increased supply chain/critical mineral resilience. We analyze key announcements and investment implications.

items.title: U.S. Semiconductors: AI Infra Summit Day 2 Takeaways
items.summary: For Day 2 of the AI Infra Summit we focus on networking-specific takeaways. As AI workloads become more reasoning-intensive and context-rich, infrastructure scaling will also depend on innovations across memory hierarchies, HBM, system architectures, and networking fabrics.

items.title: India Economics: Enhancing Savings and Investments
items.summary: We offer a scenario analysis to project India's savings and investments requirements over the next decade and identify the financing gap. We explore some policy issues concerning household savings, at an aggregate level as well as regarding allocation toward different asset classes.

items.title: Australia Banks: A Stronger Investment Cycle
items.summary: We expect a multi-year period of elevated business investment in Australia's "two-speed economy," which should support business credit growth. The growing split between business and housing growth highlights the relative valuation attractiveness of NAB, which we're upgrading to Buy.

items.title: Fed Raises Rates 25 Basis Points, With a Hawkish Tone
items.summary: Details of the FOMC meeting, including a unanimous 25-basis-point rate hike and a median “dot” showing one more such hike this year, were close to our and market expectations. We offer further analysis in this note.  In our base case, the Fed resumes rate cuts in June.

items.title: Global Equity Strategy: The Fed and the Long End
items.summary: Risks from more restrictive monetary policy have compounded worries about higher long-end bond yields. So will higher yields derail the bull market in equities? We analyze the historical record and explore why it suggests more short-term caution amid stagflationary risks from geopolitics.

items.title: Oil Monitor: Uncertain Times
items.summary: Saudi Arabia's shutdown of the East-West pipeline highlighted that regional energy infrastructure remains vulnerable and risks are no longer confined to the Strait of Hormuz. Recent strong price action has also been supported by physical-market strength beyond geopolitical headlines.

items.title: U.S. Semiconductors: AI Infra Summit Day 1 Takeaways
items.summary: Our takeaways from Day 1 of the AI Infra Summit include that fundamentally, frontier AI model developers see AI safety and alignment as a compute-intensive process. This implies that — contrary to investor worries — safety concerns may drive more, rather than less, demand for compute.

items.title: Emerging Markets El Niño Monthly Tracker
items.summary: We look at emerging-markets rainfall forecasts for the rest of the year. EM food inflation momentum rose toward its recent averages, with more pronounced pick-ups in EM Asia, Nigeria and Chile but a very benign picture in Mexico, central and eastern Europe, and Israel.

items.title: Brazil Elections and the Need for Fiscal Reforms
items.summary: With the presidential election near, we look at Brazil's need for fiscal reforms, as some sort of adjustment in the next administration seems unavoidable. In this third report, we explain why we believe Brazil may benefit from a HR reform that changes the labor regime of public servants.

items.title: What's Behind Our AB-InBev Target Price Increase
items.summary: We believe the market underappreciates AB-InBev’s BEES platform, assigning little value to its Marketplace ecosystem. We value it at $17.9bn (€8/share), forecast $13.4bn gross merchandise value and $1.2bn EBITDA by 2030, and raise our price target to €93. We reiterate our Buy rating.

items.title: Prediction Markets: SCOTUS Path Becoming Clearer
items.summary: We hosted a call with legal expert Daniel Wallach on the battle between states and prediction market operators such as Kalshi. He expects the Supreme Court to take the issue, sees states as more likely to prevail, and believes investors misread the implications. We agree.

items.title: China Consumer: Positive Gold Jewelry Readthrough from Laopu Survey
items.summary: Citi’s survey of affluent Chinese consumers reinforces our positive outlook on the high-end gold jewelry market. Laopu shows strong loyalty and repurchase intent, with scope to expand its customer base. Our top pick in the China gold jewelry space is Laopu, followed by CTF and Luk Fook.

items.title: Equity Markets Positioning Deteriorates as Investors Rebuild Shorts
items.summary: Global equity positioning weakened further last week as investors adopted a more defensive stance and bearish flows re-emerged across major markets. Renewed shorts building across the US, Europe and parts of Asia drove a broad-based deterioration in sentiment. We discuss the risks herein.

items.title: UK Economics: BoE Preview
items.summary: We expect the MPC to keep rates unchanged in September with a 6-3 split, but have revised up our Bank Rate forecast to include 25bps hikes in 2026Q4 and 2027Q1. External inflation pressures have once again assailed the UK economy, which we think will force a policy response from the Bank.

items.title: Are Calls for Slower AI an Attempt to Shape Regulation?
items.summary: We see AI labs' calls for slower frontier AI development as likely sincere but also driven by a desire to shape the regulatory framework before an AI incident prompts a broader and potentially less technically informed response. We consider the potential impacts of such a slowdown herein.

items.title: Why France's 2027 Presidential Elections Matter
items.summary: We offer an overview of France's upcoming presidential elections with a roadmap of the process and analysis of the stakes for markets. We see only two likely victors: Rassemblement National leader Marine Le Pen or a centrist candidate, with legislative elections likely to follow shortly.

items.title: Global Athletic Survey: Local Brands Gain Ground in China
items.summary: Our quarterly consumer athletic survey found Nike gaining or holding its position vs. Adidas across regions, with Adidas dropping most significantly in China. In China, local brands Li Ning and Anta moved up the ranks and closed the gap vs. Nike, while the Jordan brand improved in China.

items.title: U.S. Industrial Conglomerates: Calls for the Fall
items.summary: We remain constructive on Multi-Industrials into year's end, seeing Multis and E&Cs with good visibility to growth supported by data-center tailwinds as well positioned. We also see good potential in shorter-cycle-exposed Multis with accelerating growth. We spotlight key names herein.

items.title: Debate of the Day: The IAA Truck Show and Chinese BEV Risks
items.summary: A key debate at the IAA Truck show in Hannover concerns Chinese BEV risks in Europe and Latin America. We consider the bears' arguments for a big market-share loss for European names, including major margin pressure, and the key impediments we see to such margin pressure.

items.title: Ten Internet Takeaways From Our Global TMT Conference
items.summary: We highlight 10 key takeaways for Internet names from our Global TMT Conference. We emerge incrementally positive on broader secular trends, particularly across Online Advertising, eCommerce and Cloud demand, as AI product development benefits and efficiencies become clearer.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence: Reasserting the Western Frontier
items.summary: Our Global TMT Conference saw enterprise AI adoption diverging between compute-intensive frontier reasoning and lower-cost open deployments optimized for repeatable tasks. The dynamics favor names that pair efficient model routing with control over proprietary context and learning loops.

items.title: Monitoring AI's Impact on IT Services
items.summary: Discussions at our Global TMT Conference concerned AI as the major driver changing IT delivery. Productivity gains are tangible but often revenue-deflationary, accelerating a shift away from headcount-linked revenue toward fixed-fee and outcome-based models. We consider the impacts herein.

items.title: Global Semiconductors: Continual Learning to Fuel Demand
items.summary: We think continual learning in AI will drive memory demand across diverse products including HBM, server DDR5 and eSSDs, leading to memory undersupply worsening throughout 2028 and persisting into 2031. In this Deep Dive we highlight names we see as major potential beneficiaries.

items.title: Africa Weekly: What's Next in Senegal and Nigeria?
items.summary: We explore unresolved policy issues facing Senegal despite its decision to move onto an IMF program and seek debt “re-profiling.” We also consider Nigeria’s food price inflation problem and what it may imply for monetary policy going forward into 2027.

items.title: U.S. Rates Weekly: Is a Hike the Antidote?
items.summary: Friday’s CPI print may be the perfect antidote to the long-end UST fever. Implied core PCE is high enough to warrant a Fed hike, but the details imply a more grounded neutral rate. We continue to like the risk-reward of the 20y bond here. We offer further analysis and strategies herein.

items.title: PULSE Monitor: Remembrance
items.summary: I remember the confusion, realization and horror as 9/11 unfolded; 25 years later, its butterfly effects continue. Yet the American ethos remains, with Wall Street reflecting our free enterprise system's adaptability. "Change is the only constant" is particularly true in equity markets.
